reason: The hypothesis cites no prior evidence, and its key premises—especially that repassivation kinetics govern net degradation and that microstructural refinement enhances them—are specific claims about HEA behavior that require experimental support. Standard textbook knowledge covers general passive film disruption and repassivation concepts, but not their application to HEAs under tribo-corrosion or the effect of grain size on repassivation kinetics in these alloys.
premises: Sliding wear continuously disrupts the passive oxide film on HEAs
Net degradation is controlled by the rate of oxide re-formation (repassivation)
Microstructural refinement (e.g., nano-grained structure) enhances repassivation kinetics
Faster repassivation reduces both corrosion rate and wear volume
The dynamic balance between film removal and repassivation governs tribo-corrosion response
